subject: Computer Networking
title: How Spam Filters Work
description: One-minute skill: How Spam Filters Work.

hook.text: Over 45% of all email is spam. Your inbox stays clean because filters catch it before you see it.

buildup.text: Filters score each email. High score means spam. Rules check headers, content, links, and sender reputation.

discovery.text: Bayesian filters learn from examples. Mark spam and ham, and the filter adapts to your specific patterns.

twist.text: Spammers evolve constantly. Image-based spam, zero-width characters, and homoglyph attacks bypass text filters.

climax.text: Gmail uses deep learning models trained on billions of emails. They block 99.9% of spam and phishing.

punchline.text: Spam filters score, learn, and adapt. Your inbox depends on them.

quiz.question: What does a Bayesian spam filter learn from?
options: Examples of spam and legitimate emails you mark
The time of day the email was sent

details.summary: Spam filters use a combination of content analysis, sender reputation, authentication checks, machine learning, and user behavior signals to classify email as legitimate or spam. Modern filters are highly accurate but still face an arms race with spammers who constantly evolve their techniques.
details.whyItMatters: Spam filters keep your inbox usable. Without them, over 80 percent of email traffic is spam. Understanding how they work helps you ensure your legitimate emails reach recipients.
takeaways: Filters combine content, reputation, and authentication signals
Machine learning models adapt to evolving spam patterns
Over 80% of global email traffic is spam

faq.question: Why do legitimate emails sometimes end up in spam?
faq.answer: Missing SPF, DKIM, or DMARC records trigger filters. Certain words, excessive links, or image-heavy layouts raise spam scores. New sending domains lack reputation. Shared IP addresses can inherit bad reputation from other senders. Authentication configuration is the most common fix.

faq.question: How do spammers evade filters?
faq.answer: They rotate sending domains and IPs to avoid reputation blacklists. They use image-based text to avoid content scanning. They compromise legitimate accounts to send from trusted domains. The arms race between filters and spammers drives continuous improvement on both sides.
